- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak values by 20–40% to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and forecast is low, avoid underestimating — add 10–25% to the low-end values to avoid missing rebounds.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive downward moves), model should not overreact to new sentiment spikes — dampen forecast momentum.  
- After a sharp forecast spike (e.g., >2x recent average), apply a 1–2 day lag correction — reduce the next 2–3 forecast values by 15–30% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment history shows consistent bullishness (e.g., 5+ days >0.67), model should not forecast extreme highs — cap forecast at 1.5x recent 7-day average unless sentiment confirms breakout.  
- For low-price regimes (e.g., <0.50), avoid forecasting negative values — set minimum floor at 0.05 to prevent model collapse.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), forecast should be conservative — avoid sharp directional moves unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive sentiment upturns.
